segments.text: Roll a dice sixty times, and each face should come up about ten times.
segments.caption: Roll a dice 60 times, and each face should come up about 10 times.

segments.text: But six comes up sixteen times. Is the dice unfair, or is it just luck?
segments.caption: But six comes up 16 times. Is the dice unfair, or is it just luck?

segments.text: The chi-square distribution answers that.
segments.caption: The chi-square distribution answers that.

segments.text: Here's the definition, in simple words.
segments.caption: Here's the definition, in simple words.

segments.text: Chi-square measures how far the counts we see are from the counts we expect.
segments.caption: Chi-square measures how far the counts we see are from the counts we expect.

segments.text: And the chi-square distribution shows how big that gap can get, just by luck.
segments.caption: And the chi-square distribution shows how big that gap can get, just by luck.

segments.text: A fair dice, rolled sixty times, should give ten of each face.
segments.caption: A fair dice, rolled 60 times, should give 10 of each face.

segments.text: Here's what we got: eight, nine, twelve, eleven, four, and sixteen.
segments.caption: Here's what we got: 8, 9, 12, 11, 4, and 16.

segments.text: For each face, take the gap from ten, square it, and divide by ten.
segments.caption: For each face, take the gap from 10, square it, and divide by 10.

segments.text: Squaring makes every gap positive, and makes big gaps count more.
segments.caption: Squaring makes every gap positive, and makes big gaps count more.

segments.text: Add them all up, and the chi-square score is eight point two.
segments.caption: Add them all up, and the chi-square score is 8.2.

segments.text: But even a fair dice never matches perfectly. So how big is too big?
segments.caption: But even a fair dice never matches perfectly. So how big is too big?

segments.text: Repeat the sixty rolls again and again with a fair dice, and the scores form the chi-square distribution.
segments.caption: Repeat the 60 rolls again and again with a fair dice, and the scores form the chi-square distribution.

segments.text: It starts at zero, with a long tail to the right. Its shape depends on the degrees of freedom: six faces minus one, so five.
segments.caption: It starts at zero, with a long tail to the right. Its shape depends on the degrees of freedom: six faces minus one, so five.

segments.text: For a fair dice, ninety-five percent of scores land below eleven point one.
segments.caption: For a fair dice, 95% of scores land below 11.1.

segments.text: Our score, eight point two, is inside that zone. A fair dice scores this high about fifteen percent of the time.
segments.caption: Our score, 8.2, is inside that zone. A fair dice scores this high about 15% of the time.

segments.text: So it could easily be luck. No proof the dice is unfair.
segments.caption: So it could easily be luck. No proof the dice is unfair.

segments.text: Data scientists use it to test counts everywhere: sales across the week, or what different groups of customers choose.
segments.caption: Data scientists use it to test counts everywhere: sales across the week, or what different groups of customers choose.

segments.text: So remember: chi-square compares the counts we see with the counts we expect.
segments.caption: So remember: chi-square compares the counts we see with the counts we expect.

segments.text: A small score could be luck. A score deep in the tail means something real is going on.
segments.caption: A small score could be luck. A score deep in the tail means something real is going on.

segments.text: Quick quiz!
segments.caption: Quick quiz!

segments.text: Another dice scores twenty, with the same five degrees of freedom.
segments.caption: Another dice scores 20, with the same five degrees of freedom.

segments.text: Is it fair, or suspicious?
segments.caption: Is it fair, or suspicious?

segments.text: Suspicious!
segments.caption: Suspicious!

segments.text: Twenty is far past eleven point one, deep in the tail. That almost never happens by luck.
segments.caption: 20 is far past 11.1, deep in the tail. That almost never happens by luck.
